question: Why can a full stop at the end of a one-line text message read as cold?
answer: Because in chat the send button already ends the message, so a full stop is extra, and extra marks carry meaning. Gretchen McCulloch argues that it now signals finality or flatness, the typed version of a clipped tone. The same dot at the end of a formal letter goes unnoticed: the setting charges it.
move: A signal that was once required becomes a message when it turns optional.
ask: Which habit of mine now sends a message simply because it has become optional?
reference: McCulloch, Because Internet: Understanding the New Rules of Language, Riverhead Books, 2019
